key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Rs 25,000 (screening) + Rs 5,00,000 (capitation) = Rs 5,25,000

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the reimbursement to private unaided schools under Section 12(2) for admitting EWS/DG students:
I. Reimbursement is calculated based on the per-child expenditure incurred by the State or the actual amount charged by the school, whichever is less.
II. If the school receives land or equipment at concessional rates, it may not be entitled to full reimbursement.
III. Reimbursement is provided directly by the Central Government to the private schools. Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II
II and III
I and III
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english: Reimbursement under Section 12(2) is calculated based on state per-child expenditure or actual school tuition fees, whichever is lower. If a private school receives land or equipment at concessional rates, full reimbursement may be adjusted. Reimbursements are processed directly by the appropriate State Government or local authority funding mechanisms, rather than disbursed directly by Central Government departments.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर I और II है। धारा 12(2) प्रतिपूर्ति की गणना को राज्य के प्रति-बच्चा व्यय और विद्यालय द्वारा वास्तव में ली गई राशि में से कम राशि से जोड़ती है। जहाँ विद्यालय पहले से रियायती भूमि, भवन या उपकरण जैसी सुविधा के बदले निःशुल्क शिक्षा उपलब्ध कराने की शर्त स्वीकार कर चुका हो, वहाँ पूर्व दायित्व की सीमा तक प्रतिपूर्ति घट सकती है। तीसरा कथन गलत है, क्योंकि व्यवस्था को सीधे केंद्र सरकार द्वारा प्रत्येक विद्यालय को भुगतान के रूप में वर्णित नहीं किया गया है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Reimbursement under Section 12(2) is calculated based on state per-child expenditure or actual school tuition fees, whichever is lower. If a private school receives land or equipment at concessional rates, full reimbursement may be adjusted. Reimbursements are processed directly by the appropriate State Government or local authority funding mechanisms, rather than disbursed directly by Central Government departments.

questions.question_english: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a "good test" in the context of evaluation procedures prescribed under Section 29?

questions.explanation_english: Section 29 emphasizes objective, non- threatening evaluation through Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation (CCE). key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Subjectivity

Section 29 emphasizes objective, non- threatening evaluation through Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation (CCE). A good evaluation test must possess high statistical reliability, construct validity, and scoring objectivity. questions.question_english: An 11-year-old child, who has never attended school, is admitted to Class 6 (age-appropriate class). However, the child cannot read or write. As per the RTE Act, what must the school do?
options_english: Provide special training to bring the child on par, keeping them integrated in Class 6.
Demote the child to foundational Class 1 until basic literacy and numeracy are demonstrated.
Expel the child from regular school on the grounds that they cannot cope with Class 6 curriculum.

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 4, an 11-year-old child must be admitted directly to Class 6, which is their age- appropriate grade. questions.question_english: What is the most appropriate reason why unaided private schools are exempted from forming an SMC under Section 21, but are instead required to form a different committee under state rules?
options_english: They are self-funded and governed by trust rules, preserving structural autonomy while meeting RTE norms.
Private unaided schools are statutorily exempt from admitting any children residing in the local neighbourhood.
